title: Two language-scoring controls missed their frozen rules
question: Did two archived language-scoring searches satisfy their own frozen positive-control rules?
reader_question: Did these language searches validate their scoring controls?
summary: Both sources report 20,480 manuscript decodes, but neither saved control meets its preregistered advantage-over-English test. Each program used a different comparison to proceed.
finding: Four language-specific models all tied English at 24/24 plants under the frozen own-null detection-rate rule; the program instead passed them by d-prime. A separate orthography-matched English scorer also tied ordinary English under its frozen rule on Latin, Greek and vowel-dropped English; its program passed Latin via an OR with a fixed-score-bar comparison. Neither reported zero-survivor manuscript grid is control-validated under its original rule.
limitations: This independently checks pinned plans, decision code and saved control summaries from two source lanes. Neither planted simulation nor either reported 20,480-case manuscript grid was locally rerun. An orthography-matched English scorer is not a Latin or Greek language model; no actual plaintext language is established.
next_steps: Freeze controls with power to reveal a detection-rate advantage and use one unchanged rule before rerunning and calibrating the complete search.

scope.representation: Two pinned Dukotah source-control audits: R24-C1-ext four language-specific models and R24-C1 matched-runic orthography-adjusted English scorer. Each has a frozen plan, decision code and saved 24-plant control summaries. No manuscript grid was locally rerun.
scope.procedure: Verify source file hashes; recompute each frozen own-null power decision and the different executed decision from all eligible saved control summaries; distinguish the two scoring models and compare their source verdicts.
scope.parameters: R24-C1-ext: Latin, Greek, Old English and Enochian, 24 plants and 60 wrong-key controls each. R24-C1 matched: Latin, Greek and vowel-dropped English at L=120, 24 plants each. Each source reports a separate 20,480-case LP2 grid; neither grid was locally rerun.
scope.exclusions: No conclusion about actual plaintext language, the entire key family, numeric manuscript scores, other source registers, or changed control designs. The orthography-matched English scorer is not a language-specific model.

review.reviewer: Independent saved-row and source-rule checkers for both lanes; original simulations and manuscript grids not rerun

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; source files and saved receipts from pinned Git revision are bundled.

visuals.caption: For each non-English register, both scorers found all 24 plants; the preregistered rule required the own-language model to outperform English.
